name: Tap drill diameters for ISO metric coarse threads
source: ISO 2306:1972 Drills for use prior to tapping screw threads, clause 3.1 and Table 1 (coarse pitch series); pitches cross-checked with ISO 261:1998 ISO general purpose metric screw threads - General plan, Table 2 (coarse column)
verifiedFrom: https://law.resource.org/pub/in/bis/S01/is.10952.1984.pdf (IS 10952:1984, identical with ISO 2306:1972: clauses 0, 1 and 3.1, Table 1; read from the rendered page on 2026-10-22)
https://law.resource.org/pub/in/bis/S01/is.4218.2.2001.pdf (IS 4218 (Part 2):2001, identical with ISO 261:1998: clause 5, Table 2; read from the rendered pages on 2026-10-22)
verificationNotes: pitch and drill were read from ISO 2306:1972 Table 1 (nominal diameter, pitch, minor diameter limits for 5H/6H/7H, drill diameter). Every pitch agrees with the coarse column of ISO 261:1998 Table 2.

ISO 2306:1972 Table 1 ends at M56. M60 (pitch 5.5) and M64 (pitch 6) have coarse pitches in ISO 261:1998 Table 2 but no drill in ISO 2306; they are left out (see docs/to-verify.md). Use `rule` for them only with the user's confirmation.

ISO 262 (selected sizes for bolts, screws and nuts) was not read; the sizes here are the ones ISO 2306 lists, which include second- and third-choice diameters (M1.8, M2.2, M3.5, M4.5, M7, M9, M11, ...) of ISO 261.
pitchSource: ISO 261:1998, Table 2, column 'coarse'; same values in ISO 2306:1972, Table 1
ruleSource: ISO 2306:1972, clause 1: the sizes of drills for parallel screw threads of normal length of engagement, the drill diameter being approximately equal to the nominal diameter of the thread minus the pitch
notes: ISO 2306:1972, clause 0: the hole a drill makes depends on the drill point, the material, the lubricant and the machining conditions; in soft materials the tapped minor diameter can end up smaller than the drill. The table is a guide for conventional (cutting) tapping; it does not apply to thread forming.

ISO 2306:1972, clause 1: the drill diameters, except four sizes the standard marks with an asterisk, are selected from the ISO/R 235 twist drill sizes; stocked drill diameters should be used whenever possible (clause 0).
